title: The Biggest Losers of the Year (EP. 491)

segments: Market rotation and AI bubble concerns
summary.headline: Nvidia's decline and the state of the AI trade
summary.tldr: Nvidia is facing a significant drawdown following reports of executive scandal and potential export control violations. Despite this, the S&P 500 has remained resilient, highlighting the benefits of passive indexing during periods of market volatility.

key_points.point: Nvidia is down 35% from its highs, with reports alleging the former CEO's mistress arranged to send restricted chips to China.
key_points.why_it_matters: The company's rapid growth was tied heavily to one individual, and this scandal raises questions about its future leadership and operational stability.

key_points.point: The S&P 500 index is up 9% year-to-date, with a maximum drawdown of only 9% in March.
key_points.why_it_matters: This demonstrates the resilience of a diversified index fund compared to the volatility of individual high-growth stocks.

key_points.point: Retail investors aggressively bought the dip in Nvidia, with $111 million in net buying during the first 30 minutes following the resignation news.
key_points.why_it_matters: It shows that the habit of buying the dip remains strong among retail participants despite significant negative news.

key_points.point: The weighted share of CPI components rising faster than 2% has reached 76%, the highest level since August 2022.
key_points.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation suggests the Federal Reserve may continue to hike rates, with an 85% probability of a 25 basis point increase in December.

numbers.context: Nvidia's drawdown from its recent highs as of the recording.
Nvidia's gross margin, which remains a key metric of its business strength.
The weighted share of CPI components rising faster than 2% annualized.
The market-implied probability of a 25 basis point rate hike in December.

summary.lesson: When a company's organizational structure is built entirely around one individual (key-person risk), the departure or scandal of that person can cause the company's exoskeleton to collapse faster than expected.
opinions_and_predictions: Michael believes Nvidia is 'toast' and that the market is underreacting to the scandal.
Ben believes that a recession is the only solution to bring inflation down to lower levels.
Ben suggests that the AI trade taking a breather could be a positive long-term outcome for the market.

glossary.definition: The peak-to-trough decline of an investment or fund during a specific period.
glossary.example: The S&P 500 had a maximum drawdown of 9% in March.

glossary.definition: An estimate of a company's future earnings, used to calculate the forward price-to-earnings ratio.
glossary.example: Nvidia is trading at 11 times forward earnings.

glossary.definition: A unit of measure equal to one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%).
glossary.example: There is an 85% chance of a 25 basis point rate hike.

glossary.definition: A competitive advantage that protects a company's market share and profits from rivals.
glossary.example: Ben Thompson noted Nvidia's moat was its unique organizational structure.

glossary.definition: A quarterly report that institutional investment managers must file to disclose their equity holdings.
glossary.example: The Leopold situational awareness 13F was released recently.

summary.quality_note: The hosts are financial professionals who rely on market data and news reports, though they frequently offer speculative opinions on company futures.
